scenarios.expected: Only the intended published audience reaches the item and its files; later removal takes effect. Direct links do not bypass publication/audience checks, including links to supporting Documents.
scenarios.actual: 14 recorded steps passed with Nadia Haddad publishing (the first is an API fixture, one is a limitation check). While Draft and while published Legal Only, Daniel Okafor also opened the record, and Mei Tanaka and Sara Haddadi got 404 from the article read and were returned to /portal. Mei was sent from /knowledge and the record to /portal, and the staff list, read and publish calls answered 403. Audience offered Legal Only and Everyone; Everyone and Knowledge Item actions, Publish removed Draft and showed On the portal. No Portal link existed until Daniel used Settings, Intake, Deflection links, Add link. Its Knowledge item list offered the item but not the draft, archived or published Legal Only fixtures. Mei followed the link under Before you submit and saw Documents before Guidance, primary first. She downloaded all three files byte for byte and had no staff or Version controls. Daniel then used Actions, Mark confidential on one supporting file, and the row showed CONFI (spoken "Confidential"). Mei's article then listed two files. The saved address of the Confidential file answered 404 for both readers, the same as a missing item, while the other two answered 200. Nadia saw no row for it and her Documents list left it out. Clear confidential mark brought it back for Mei and Nadia. A guidance edit and a new primary Version reached Mei with no second Publish. Audience Legal Only opened Remove this from the portal? reading "1 deflection link points at this item". Cancel kept Everyone and Continue saved Legal Only. The link left the Portal home, the saved article address returned to /portal, and the article and all three saved file addresses answered 404 for both readers (8 denied reads). The link stayed in Settings. Everyone restored access. Unpublish (same dialog) returned Draft and blocked access, and Publish restored the existing link. The list had no archived toggle. Archive with Replaced by kept guidance and Documents, disabled Title, Type, Folder and Audience, and blocked the link, article and files with no redirect to the replacement. The saved staff address reopened it, and Restore returned Published, Everyone and working downloads. Replaced by did not offer an archived item. It offered an item created in another session without a reload. When that choice was archived while the dialog was open, Archive showed "The replacement must be a live Knowledge Item." and the item stayed live. With no session the article went to /portal/login and the article and files answered 401.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the technical reviewer; not a human user study and not the feature owner's approval.

The registry's out-of-audience comparison reader has no per-person equivalent: a Knowledge audience is Legal Only or Everyone, and Everyone means every signed-in Portal session. The walkthrough compared two Business Portal readers against the item in Draft, published Legal Only, unpublished and archived states, against a browser with no session (/portal/login, 401), and against a Confidential supporting Document (404 on the Portal, absent for the Legal Team Member).

Marking a Knowledge Document Confidential was done by the Administrator, as the guide says. The walkthrough confirmed the author's product bug. The Legal Team Member who uploaded a Knowledge Document is offered Mark confidential. After she uses it the Document leaves her staff record after a reload, and her own clear request answers 404. Only an Administrator returned it.
MCP Knowledge reads for a Business User were not exercised; MCP and API keys start off and need configure-mcp setup. The guide's MCP sentence rests on the author's source review.

The work2 lab is shared with other DOC-030 agents. Only records named DOC-030 knowledge V-C34 were created. The run added three deflection links and removed them at the end, and archived its published fixtures. It changed no organization setting. Two development runs before the recorded run (stamps 20260925T1029 and 20260925T1035) are not credited; see harnessNotes in the log.

The publication fixtures (items, Documents, guidance, replacement, archived and Legal Only items, and the late replacement) were created through the API. The guide's own controls were used for Audience, Publish, Unpublish, Archive, Restore, the deflection links, Mark confidential and Clear confidential mark, the guidance edit and the new Version. The competing archive of the late replacement came from the second staff session through the API.
